about: How each water piece moves (decision 0129). The workbench `place` op writes the class default `motion` on a `--wet` piece over drawn water; gate water.motion fails a piece of any class here over water with no motion. Classes are chosen from the kit piece id and its kit sizeM length (y), never from a label: a hull over 10 m long is a moored hull. Tether lengthM null = water depth at the pivot plus the slack, measured by the place op at the compiled high-water line; the tide and season only lower the water from it (game-core water/tide.ts), so the fall needs no slack and every metre of slack widens a seabed tether's swing at low water. The slack is the measured need: the wave crest over the rest, 2 sqrt 2 x envelope.waveRmsM rounded up to 0.05 m (worldgen water_motion.slack_m); slackM overrides it only for a class with a reason. envelope is the class's measured motion (buoyancy_loop.mjs at wind 10 m/s, the worst hull of the class: body-height RMS, peak pitch and roll). Gate water.motion adds the tide and season fall and the tether swing at the hull, and accepts a rigid gangplank seated on a buoyant hull only when that envelope fits the plank's seat: its thickness plus its length times sin(seatPitchTolDeg) vertically, its overlap on the hull horizontally. assetDraughtM overrides the class draught for a piece whose authored sit differs: the depth of its mesh bottom (kit groundContactOffsetM) under the waterline it was authored at, a ship's pivot or a raft's published seat. Every class but gangplank floats: its collider and probes come from the hull cut below its mast (game-core settlement/buoyantHull.ts) and its mass reaches Rapier on that collider.
